You control a simulated robot through the provided tools. Use the current camera images, the measured robot state, and the history of this trial to complete the user's task.

Respond with exactly one tool call per turn. Every movement call must include a brief note describing what you observe and why you choose that movement. Check the next observation before deciding your next action. A commanded target is not a measurement of the position reached.

You have at most 20 model calls for this trial, including tool errors and any done or give_up call. The trial also has a separate limit of 900 robot control steps. Call done when you judge the task complete, or give_up when you judge that you cannot complete it within the remaining budget.

Use only the supplied task, robot documentation, tools, and observations. Do not request outside assistance, access source code or hidden simulator state, or use information from other trials. No feedback or learned notes from previous trials are available.

Robot documentation:
Robot: one Franka Panda arm with a parallel-jaw gripper in a tabletop simulation. The table surface is at world z=0.80 m. World +z points upward. All position targets and measured end-effector positions use the same world frame.

The move_to tool accepts absolute x, y, z, yaw, and gripper targets. Position units are meters and yaw units are radians. Valid bounds are x in [-0.30, 0.35], y in [-0.30, 0.30], z in [0.80, 1.30], and yaw in [-pi, pi]. The gripper is oriented approximately downward; yaw is its controllable rotation about world +z. Pitch and roll are not exposed as action dimensions.

Gripper commands are binary: use 0 to close and 1 to open. The reported gripper value is the measured opening normalized from 0 to 1, so holding an object may produce an intermediate measurement. In the adapter, targets below 0.35 latch closed, targets above 0.65 latch open, and intermediate targets retain the previous command. Intermediate commanded openings are not supported. Dimensions omitted from move_to are filled from the measured end-effector state by the tool layer.

The tool layer interpolates targets under its shared motion limits. The robot may not reach a target before the next observation; use the measured state and images to determine what happened. No additional settling motion is inserted after a tool call.

State fields: eef_pos is the measured end-effector position; eef_quat uses (w,x,y,z); eef_yaw is in radians; gripper is measured normalized opening; eef_state is [x,y,z,yaw,gripper]. joint_pos and joint_vel describe the seven arm joints in radians and radians per second. joint_eff contains arm actuator torques in N m, including controller compensation; it is not a fingertip contact sensor.

Cameras: front and side are fixed views; wrist moves with the hand. All are 224x224 RGB images with the top row at the top of the view. The wrist view can rotate as the hand rotates. No fixed mapping from image directions to world x/y is assumed. Each request includes the current three views and retains images from at most the two most recent observations.
Goal: Pick up the red block from the table and place it inside the blue bowl.

function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "One policy call remains and the red block is still resting on the table (last seen in the side view beside the bowl near wall at about x=0.104, y=0.005), not inside the bowl. The hand is at (0.1067, 0.000, 0.8628) with the gripper closed on air (measured opening 0.018), so a grasp, a transport over the bowl mouth and a release cannot be finished in the remaining call. I am not claiming the goal was reached.", "hindsight": "Concrete facts measured in this trial. (1) Chunk length: the move_to step count is set by the largest normalised delta including the gripper dimension, so re-issuing gripper=0 or gripper=1 from the opposite extreme buys 40-79 step chunks (2-4 s) while a small pure Cartesian move gives only 1-3 steps; the arm does reach the commanded pose when the chunk is long, and lags about 1 cm per 3-step chunk otherwise. (2) The gripper stroke is slow, roughly 0.006-0.012 normalised per step, so a full open-to-close needs on the order of 60-120 control steps: plan at least two long chunks for a close. (3) The red block is about 4 cm across: a genuine grip stalls the measured opening near 0.50-0.52 and then holds through lift and transport; if the reading keeps falling past 0.4 down to 0.02-0.3 the pads closed on air. (4) Fingertip geometry: the pads sit roughly 0-4.5 cm below the reported eef_pos, so grasping a block on the z=0.80 table wants eef z about 0.82-0.86, and pushing the z command to the 0.80 clamp makes the fingers jam on the table and skids the hand sideways in y (I saw a 1.4 cm -y drift that cost the grasp). (5) Cameras: in the wrist view image-up is world +x and image-right is -y, and the block must be judged against the finger gap rather than the frame centre because the optical axis is offset forward; the two fixed cameras show almost no parallax for hand motion in x, so absolute x should be taken from the measured eef_pos plus the wrist view, not from them. (6) Layout: the block started near x=-0.045, y=0 and the bowl is centred near y=0 with its near wall around x=0.12; releasing at x=0.104 left the block on the table touching the outside of that wall, so the drop point needs to be nearer x=0.15-0.17 to clear the rim. (7) Budget: six calls spent localising the block was too many; the fast route is open wide, drive straight down onto the block with gripper=0 latched, confirm the opening stalls near 0.5, lift, translate over the bowl centre, then open."}

content: give_up: One policy call remains and the red block is still resting on the table (last seen in the side view beside the bowl near wall at about x=0.104, y=0.005), not inside the bowl. The hand is at (0.1067, 0.000, 0.8628) with the gripper closed on air (measured opening 0.018), so a grasp, a transport over the bowl mouth and a release cannot be finished in the remaining call. I am not claiming the goal was reached.
